I don't want to be offensive, but all these complaints on Black Annis
and Mitru seems to be nothing more than excuses to avoid admitting
they're pretty solid and worth buying. Many players would be more
comfortable to indulge in rightful complain about grouping if the
vamps were next to unusable or totally ineffective when mixed with
older minions, meaning "I do not feel tempted to buy them". Since
almost all offer new possibilities and the rest offer sensible
variation of already existing strategies, accepting them for what they
are would mean accepting the grouping rule. But then what would remain
to complain about? The banning of KR and DU?

Messages.Author: Teemu T Vilen
Messages.Body:
"Fabio \"Sooner\" Macedo" <fa...@cohesp.com.br> wrote:
: On 10 Feb 2005 07:37:35 -0800, pd...@lightlink.com wrote:
: I don't want to be offensive, but all these complaints on Black Annis

: and Mitru seems to be nothing more than excuses to avoid admitting
: they're pretty solid and worth buying.

Annis and Mitru are both solid Vampires when it comes to their
disciplines and specialties. Mitru, being one of the npc characters I
kind of liked in Transylvanian Chronicles, is pretty nice altogether,
from Disciplines to the picture. Of course, if you complain him to
Miller, without the +1 str Mitru will just never be as good as Miller in
what Miller does best - and I guess that's what most are muttering. He
has for for prevent, animalism for DotB and with the !Gangrel path he
plays Blur + Claws for free.

Black Annis, on the other hand is more of a rip-off. Annis, Beast.. both
!nossies, except Annis has the no-brainer protean and she's better in
rite about everything else. What I hate though, is the picture, which
reminds me mostly of bad Tales from the Crypt cover art that tried very
hard to look like B-rated camp. I'd hate dumping Beast for Annis, and
having to look at her.

When you play Beast it's like "Aaannd it'ssshh the Beaastrgghh!" With
Annis, I imagine it'll be closer to "*cough* I have this silly looking
cartoon !nossie here.."

Small gripe. Would've liked her to no end without David Day's school
grade artwork.

In general you are partly right when it comes to me. I haven't played
too much with group 4. Mostly because from my POV it would require some
heavy investment into the cards (not that I didn't buy a lot of them
already) and the options I have with group 4 just aren't worth it. Maybe
after a few more expansions when I have accumulated enough of them and
get tired of them gathering dust.

//T

I couldn't agree more on the Black Annis art issue. But I'm one of the
few who actually like most of Christopher Shy's artwork for WW, so I
won't expect anyone to adhere to my aesthetics. We've had plenty of
different art styles on V:TES, from anime-inspired library cards to
general photoshop enhancement and pulp-book cover illustration, so I
gave up on that issue long ago. What I can expect in that regard is
that the publishers are the first ones to be desire a clear and
uniform art between expansions, but that is just not possible given
issues like artist availability, time schedule and such. That would
make me feel more resigned on the art mess that is V:TES.

If you won't mind a little suggestion... Go Anarch! :)

That's what I do to most 3/4 vamps I do have when I note that I don't
have a proper crypt available to go monoclan. Note that I'm nowhere
near completing the Camarilla set when it comes to crypt cards yet.
Going anarch serves the purpose of putting them to good use right now.
But of course, that depends on how much one is willing to be beaten up
by more focused decks until it finds some balance between anarch cards
and "normal" ones. Myself, I don't mind losing horribly 4 times if in
the fifth I can pull something threatening with anarchs in the fifth
game...

I must confess though, that Mitru is a borderline case. He is clearly
a City Gangrel, works fine in that capacity, and as such his extra
disciplines are not a problem at all. The problem - as I see it - are
those vampires who aren't really either City or Country (but pay for
the disciplines of both division).

hasty in including him in the same basket as Harry Reese and Maria
Stone lie in.
